meta.title: HTTPS: What Happens When You Visit google.com

views.label: Google got certified
views.note: Before you visit: Google generates a key pair and gets a CA to sign a certificate for google.com.

views.label: Your browser arrives
views.note: Your browser opens a connection. Google responds with a certificate that carries its public key and the CA's signature.

views.label: Check the certificate
views.note: The browser checks the CA's signature against trusted root keys it already ships with — no network call needed.

views.label: Session key and encrypted traffic
views.note: A session key is encrypted with Google's public key and sent. From here on, everything is symmetric-encrypted.

messages.label: signed certificate: public key + google.com
messages.note: Google generated keys, then asked the CA to sign

messages.label: ServerHello + Certificate: here is my public key
messages.note: carries Google's public key and the CA's signature

messages.label: verify: did you sign this cert?
messages.note: checked locally — your browser ships with the CA's key

messages.label: session key (encrypted with your public key)
messages.note: only Google's private key can decrypt this

messages.label: encrypted traffic — symmetric from here
messages.note: both sides now share the session key

cards.title: How HTTPS really works
items: Before you visit: Google generates a key pair and gets a CA to sign a certificate
When you arrive: Google sends the certificate with its public key and CA signature
Your browser verifies the signature against trusted root keys it ships with
A session key travels encrypted with Google's public key — then everything is symmetric
